---
name: speed-reading
description: >-
  Produce ALG Four paragraph-index annotations from approved bilingual articles:
  concise Traditional Chinese explanation, complete English chunk/stress reading,
  cognitive skeleton and source-supported Active practice. Preserve source meaning and bytes.
---

# Cognitive Linguistics & Speed-Reading Engine

Transform supplied English into a **Dual-Layer Streamlined Annotated Text**.
Aim for easier scanning and lower avoidable reading effort. This is a reading
layout hypothesis: do not promise faster comprehension, one fixation per chunk,
eliminated regression, or reduced working memory without reader measurements.
Original wording, punctuation, quantities, code, conditions, negation and causal
scope remain intact. The skeleton supplements the paragraph; it never replaces it.

## Annotation Owner and input

**speed-reading owns the annotation content shown in the ALG Four article index.**
Read the complete approved English and Traditional Chinese article, not just the
current heading. For every aligned prose paragraph/blockquote, produce its concise
Traditional Chinese explanation with exact English technical terms, complete
English reading projection, short cognitive skeleton and any source-supported
Active terms, production sentences and self-expression cue/oracle.

[alg-four](../alg-four/SKILL.md) supplies the paired source identity and existing
manifest contract, binds paragraph anchors, validates coverage and renders the
index. It consumes this skill's annotations; it does not independently author a
second annotation set. `leetcode-mental` retains article meaning and `medium-writing`
retains assembly. The source article is never rewritten by annotation work.

Follow [the existing annotation contract](../alg-four/references/lesson-contract.md)
for paragraph/decision links, exact original Git blobs, overlapping Passive/Active
roles and cumulative admission. A primary source quote is not the complete causal
proof. If a sentence/oracle uses another paragraph's premise or cost derivation,
bind each supporting paragraph and exact English quote and expose its link. Keep
operation count, aggregate work and cost conditions together; do not fill an
absent argument from the author's private knowledge. Return a missing premise to
the article Owner instead of silently fixing it in a note.

Active words must help explain an actual decision/runtime fact, with a faithful
complete English sentence and source-bound cue/oracle. No per-article quota,
mechanical vocabulary harvesting or inferred learner mastery. Review the complete
meaning before applying the display rules below. Review data and uncertainty
belong in the existing evidence/sidecar, not copyable prose. Source identity is
not semantic proof. Existing approved annotations may be retained as legacy
inputs; changing the Owner contract does not relabel them as newly generated.

## Outer layer: syntax before word count

- Insert `/` before a prepositional, participial or infinitive phrase when it
  preserves attachment and makes the sentence easier to follow. Prefer roughly
  3–5 words per visual chunk where syntax allows; never split a tight unit merely
  to meet that target. A chunk is not an observed ocular fixation.
- Insert `//` at a meaningful major clause boundary and **immediately follow it
  with a line break**. Relative/subordinate clauses and a long subject/predicate
  boundary are candidates, not automatic rules. Keep a condition with its scope;
  do not make a dependent claim look unconditional.
- Enclose a genuine lexical bundle, idiom or tight modifier in `[ ]` when useful.
  Do not bracket every chunk or split a source identifier, formula or literal.
- Existing slashes, brackets, Markdown/code syntax and technical identifiers are
  source characters. Preserve them distinctly from added annotation markers.

## Inner layer: primary stress, not first letters

- Bold **only the orthographic span representing the primary stressed syllable**
  of a content word: noun, main verb, adjective or key adverb in this sentence.
- Check the word's pronunciation, grammatical role and intended sense using an
  authoritative pronunciation source. Keep the URL/entry, pronunciation and
  reviewed spelling span in the existing evidence. Phonetic syllables do not
  always map unambiguously to spelling; leave an uncertain span plain.
- Never derive stress from word length, the first letters, or another word's
  suffix. Do not copy unverified stress examples from a prompt as authority.
  A checked example is `**al**gorithm` (Cambridge `/ˈæl.ɡər.ɪ.ðəm/`).
- Do not insert syllable dots or hyphens into words. Keep their original shape.
  A one-syllable content word may be fully bold only when its role is appropriate.
- Leave articles, prepositions, auxiliaries/modals, conjunctions and pronouns
  plain. Optional backticks may recede a structural lead-in; do not suppress
  negation or scope cues. Do not bold a form of *have* merely because it looks
  like a main verb elsewhere; determine its role here.
- If stress evidence is absent, retain faithful plain English for that word.
  This fallback preserves meaning; it is not a claim of verified prosody.

## Output and review

For a direct English-text request, output only this transformed text and skeleton;
no explanations, analysis or verification report. For ALG Four, save these two
parts in the existing paragraph annotation along with the required Traditional
Chinese explanation and any admitted Active content; the rendered reading block
uses the same template:

### 【極速流暢標註文本】
[Complete source paragraph with the reviewed annotation marks]

---
* **極簡認知骨架**：`[Core Node 1]` → `[Core Action/Node 2]` → `[Core Node 3]`

The standalone template retains a 10–15-word cognitive cue. In the ALG Four
adapter, label it **閱讀提示（非獨立結論）** and use a short question or topic chain
that tells the reader what to inspect. Do not compress a theorem into an
unqualified verdict. No reader should need to infer that a cue supplies proof.

The acceptance unit is the **complete paragraph annotation**, including its
source-bound context and any linked premises, not the short cue alone. For each
annotation save `reading_context` with:

- `premises`: one or more concise Traditional Chinese statements specifying the
  applicable input, selected object, quantifier, representation or cost assumption.
  Each has `text` and `supporting_sources` containing paragraph indices and exact
  English quotes. Link other paragraphs when the current paragraph depends on them.
- `checkpoint`: a statement with the same source bindings when a result depends
  on observation time, loop boundary, completed updates or operation order; use
  null when no state/ordering checkpoint is needed. Do not invent a temporal rule
  for a purely descriptive paragraph.

Keep the complete English and concise explanation visible with these conditions;
15 words constrain only the reading cue, never the premises or proof. The UI must
show the conditions/checkpoint before the cue. A reader follows the linked source
when a note depends on a derivation elsewhere. An absent source argument remains
an article-Owner issue; adding a note cannot invent it.

Review the *whole annotation*, including retained notes and Active text, rather
than only paraphrasing its main topic. Compare its factual assertions with the
source in both directions: an example or sufficient mechanism does not establish
an exclusive or necessary mechanism. For words such as only, must and cannot,
check whether the source licenses that strength; try a different legal mechanism
that produces the same effect. Narrow the statement to its actual scope if the
reverse implication fails. Then distinguish each licensed conclusion from a
nearby illegal inference by changing an input assumption, selected set, cost model
or observation checkpoint. Require a reader to quote the explicit context/source
that licenses each distinction. A cited paragraph's existence is
not enough: the displayed explanation must say why its premise matters. Record
missing conditions and counterexamples before repair. If repeated attempts fail,
stop and reconsider the representation or acceptance unit rather than adding
another exhortation or silently supplying the missing premise while scoring.
A bounded fresh Reader result does not establish general stability or human benefit.

Before handing the complete annotation back to ALG Four, recover the original text by removing
only **added** marks, and compare it to the complete approved paragraph. Independently
check clause attachment, bundles, every bold stress span, full-annotation scope
and checkpoint, and that the cue does not assert an unsupported conclusion. A lossless comparison cannot prove those semantic judgments. If a
needed pronunciation or reading observation is unavailable, record that gap in
the existing evidence and use the plain-word fallback; do not fabricate PASS.

Pronunciation reference: [Cambridge algorithm](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/pronunciation/english/algorithm).
Evidence limit: [Rayner et al., 2016](https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100615623267)
reviews the speed/comprehension trade-off; it does not validate this layout.

---
name: alg-four
description: Integrate speed-reading annotations into a source-bound right-hand article index with paragraph anchors, admission validation and reading navigation. Preserve complete original Medium content and four encounters without rewriting it.
---

# ALG Four — annotate original articles, never rewrite them

## Owners

- [leetcode-mental](../leetcode-mental/SKILL.md) owns the original coding problem and **complete article semantic content** under its [complete-article profile](../leetcode-mental/references/article-content-profile.md), including decisions, invariant, runtime, code, proof and constraints. Ordinary v4 teaching retains its original scope.
- [medium-writing](../medium-writing/SKILL.md) owns **Medium layout and exact-edition assembly** for the selected complete-article profile; other writing routes retain their existing ownership. The accepted original article stays byte-identical when ALG Four projects its notes.
- [speed-reading](../speed-reading/SKILL.md) owns **article-index annotation content**: every paragraph's Traditional Chinese explanation, complete English chunk/stress reading, cognitive skeleton and source-supported Passive/Active production sentences, cues and oracles. It reviews semantic support across the complete paired article; the source body remains immutable.
- **alg-four** owns the **source-bound annotation integration**: paired source identity, one-to-one coverage, admission validation, paragraph anchors, right-hand index navigation and rendering. It receives speed-reading's content in the existing sidecar rather than authoring another annotation set. It does not own a rewritten article, new Writer, LMS, CLI stage or second Router.

[alg-vocab-encounter](../alg-vocab-encounter/SKILL.md) remains the passive lexical-practice leaf. Historical [cefr-alg-four-pass](../cefr-alg-four-pass/SKILL.md), its 12-file upstream Git Blob lock, frozen lessons and original CEFR session oracle gate remain unchanged.

## Cumulative 2000 Active terms and 2000 related sentences

This is a cross-article, deduplicated **target corpus**, NOT a requirement to find two thousand words inside one LeetCode explanation.

An Active lexical item must satisfy every admission condition:
1. It is necessary or reusable for explaining a **real decision, invariant, canonical identity, state transition or underlying runtime mechanism** from the source.
2. It has an exact source-article identity and paragraph index; the term or its meaning is actually supported by that paragraph.
3. It helps an engineer independently *produce* an explanation in precise English, not merely recognize a rare word.
4. It has at least one fully formed English sentence faithful to the same original technical claim, actor, condition, negation and consequence.
5. A source-bound question or meaning oracle can distinguish an accurate response from a superficially fluent one.
6. Repeated terms with equivalent meanings across articles share one corpus identity; record more contexts, do not inflate the distinct count.

The wider **Passive** inventory covers encounter and recognition. Classify each original article paragraph as `PASSIVE` or `PASSIVE_AND_ACTIVE`; the same core concept may be encountered receptively and later generated actively. The labels are practice roles, not grammatical passive/active voice and not achievements. Reject nonsource filler rather than manufacturing 2000 entries.

## Four cognitive encounters, always on the SAME original paragraphs

1. Encounter the actual original paragraph, notice term form, sound and the short zh-TW meaning annotation with original English technical terms.
2. Revisit that same paragraph and recognize the engineering decision and its word-to-runtime link.
3. Re-read or listen to the **same** paragraph with original context and trace its invariant, actor, branch or state change.
4. Without copying the original, generate an English sentence and decision explanation; compare to the source-bound oracle after an authentic attempt.

These are **four operations over the same prose**, not `pass1/pass2/pass3` replacement texts or separate rewritten sections. A published site may expose a non-tracking expandable prompt/oracle in the **right-hand section/paragraph outline**, linked to the unmodified source paragraph. It is not a native CEFR Session. That older UI still requires an acknowledged attempt before reveal and a distinct reported comparison event.

Every original prose paragraph/blockquote must have exactly one source-bound **sidecar entry** in the right-hand hierarchical outline, accessible by a stable paragraph anchor. Expand the current section/subsection and paragraph entry as reading position changes; clicking outline headings or paragraph entries navigates to the original article. Keep headings, paragraph sequence, code, technical semantics, original article facts and word choice **unchanged**. The speed-reading Owner makes annotation decisions from the entire article, not a quota of exactly five; include the original engineering claims throughout. Notes must be concise Traditional Chinese with the canonical English terms intact and tied to an actual decision and the paragraph's subject.

## Right-hand source-preserving reading projection

The site must first receive one approved, **complete** article from the selected
`leetcode-mental → medium-writing` route. `alg-four` reads that pinned source and
projects annotations **alongside**, never into, the article. It may continue to
display the currently pinned original sample until an approved replacement article
is available; a Skill change alone does not prove that a new article was authored.

For the complete LeetCode article profile, require an approved English source
that aligns **one-to-one with the current Traditional Chinese prose paragraphs**.
Validate both original Git blobs, rendered heading and paragraph structure,
protected code and all section/figure placements before emitting any annotations.
A changed paragraph or edition requires source re-review and a newly pinned
manifest; decision-level English summaries cannot silently replace paragraph
English in Mode C.

Build the outline from actual Markdown heading levels (H1/H2/H3/H4 as supported by
the local renderer) and the exact paragraphs that follow them. Every paragraph
has a stable anchor and one annotation; click a heading/paragraph to jump.
Scrolling expands the active headline, subheadline and paragraph note and
collapses unrelated branches. Keep the complete article centered. At the middle
right, a normally closed rail has one bar per top-level chapter (including the
introduction), with bar length proportional to that chapter's rendered text and
an explicit chapter/paragraph count in the expanded panel. The selected bar
reflects reading position, not completion. Hover or button activation opens a
scrollable contents-and-notes dialog; touch and keyboard must also work without
hover. Escape/close restores the trigger's focus. Navigating to a heading must
select its first following paragraph, rather than a note in the preceding chapter.
Do not infer reading completion or record learning events from viewport tracking.

**Active**: render speed-reading’s admitted lexical items yellow within the expanded annotation
entry, with the bound English production sentence and optional recall/oracle.
Yellow is a visual training cue, not measured mastery.

**Passive Mode C**: consume the repository [speed-reading Owner](../speed-reading/SKILL.md)'s
annotation for the complete aligned English paragraph. Its dual-layer result and short
cognitive skeleton belong only in the expanded annotation, never the original
body. Review syntax, scope and pronunciation separately from lossless identity.
Store reviewed formatting with the existing paragraph sidecar; no model or
dictionary requests run in the browser or CI. Without reviewed formatting or
pronunciation, keep faithful plain English rather than generating mechanical
chunks or initial-letter bolding. Preserve existing approved projections until
a reviewed replacement is available.

This Mode C projection is a reading layout hypothesis, not a proven speed,
fixation, neurological or comprehension improvement. For text without verified
English stress/chunk annotations, show faithful plain English rather than
inventing phonology. The cumulative Active target and ALG Four four-encounter
policy are unchanged. A host that lacks user input/response evidence must still
say `NOT_OBSERVED`.

## Evidence and limits

The [full annotation contract](references/lesson-contract.md) defines source identity, paragraph coverage and 2000-item admission; the [Thinking Route](references/thinking-route.md) chooses only necessary cognitive interventions and the [migration](references/migration.md) preserves legacy consumers. Freeze the source Git blob; refuse a changed original or missing paragraph. `RUNTIME_TESTED`, `ACTIVE_PRACTICED`, response latency and acquired vocabulary need real runtime/learner evidence; website build and 4 available passes establish none of these.

The fourth encounter is an instructional procedure **not** a scientifically established neural consolidation threshold. No invented repetition schedule, credential, learning database, or mastery claim.

For speed-reading-authored notes, the complete annotation is the acceptance unit:
show source-bound premises and any state/order checkpoint before the short
reading cue (閱讀提示，非獨立結論). A source citation alone does not explain why
its premise matters. Follow the speed-reading Owner contract; the UI/validator
checks presence and exact bindings, while Owner/Reader review completeness.

# ALG Four source-preserving annotation and Active-2000 admission contract

The input is one approved complete article: for the selected LeetCode Medium profile, `leetcode-mental` owns all source-grounded English and zh-TW meaning and `medium-writing` assembles the approved Medium edition. `speed-reading` owns the paragraph annotation meaning (Traditional Chinese note,
English reading projection, skeleton and source-supported Active practice);
`alg-four` owns source binding, admission validation, navigation and rendering.
The exact source Markdown Git blob is immutable for annotation. A needed semantic correction belongs to the original Content Owner and must be re-admitted before the annotation is regenerated.

## Paragraph-bound output

Consume **one speed-reading-authored, source-bound Traditional Chinese/English annotation in the right-hand outline for each original prose paragraph or blockquote**, never inline beneath the article. Preserve the original English technical terms, conditions and causal links. Original HTML content must be recoverable by stripping only added anchor attributes; no insertion, reordering or mutation of source paragraphs. Do not replace article sections with four rewritten passes.

Bind every note to `source.git_blob`, a zero-based paragraph index, a source-derived decision/concept ID and one of `PASSIVE` or `PASSIVE_AND_ACTIVE`. Active and Passive semantic roles may overlap; a source paragraph can be read and rehearsed. Every Active phrase has a source paragraph and at least one complete technically correct English sentence. Each source revision requires a new reviewed manifest. If a production sentence or oracle depends on another paragraph, bind each
supporting premise as `supporting_sources` (paragraph index plus exact English
quote) on that Active item and expose navigable source links. An exact quote at
the primary anchor does not establish every cost premise or inference. Review
the complete supporting chain; do not use a heading summary as the missing proof.
Omitted or extra notes, source drift, unknown decision IDs, missing English sentences and duplicate active IDs refuse publication.

## Mode C sidecar and navigable outline

Derive major/minor heading order from the source Markdown, not a fabricated index.
Use one paragraph anchor for each rendered prose paragraph. Keep a centered
reading column and a normally closed middle-right chapter rail. Bar length
represents chapter text amount, not difficulty or mastery. Expand a scrollable
dialog on hover or explicit activation; support touch, keyboard, Escape and focus
return. Show chapter/paragraph counts, current position and the source-bound notes. Selecting an index item jumps to its source location. Scrolling follows
the active paragraph, expands only its heading/subheading ancestry, and presents
that paragraph's annotation. This UI state is not a learner observation.

Inside an expanded annotation, Active source-attested terms are highlighted
yellow beside their one or more verified production sentences. Passive content
uses a **Mode C derived reading projection**, never edits the original article:
conservative phrase-level `/` splits, `//` plus hard line breaks at meaningful
clause boundaries, `[ ]` for reviewed lexical bundles, and bold **only**
the primary stressed syllable of genuinely verified content words. Keep function
words plain; do not apply bionic initial-letter bolding or add syllable dots.
Prefer roughly 3–5 words per visual chunk only when grammar and scope permit.
If stress/segmentation evidence is absent, use faithful plain English.
For speed-reading-authored notes, render the complete source-bound
`reading_context.premises` and any `checkpoint` before a short reading cue.
Each statement has text plus exact quoted supporting paragraphs. Validate these
bindings mechanically; completeness remains an Owner/Reader judgment. Label the
cue 閱讀提示（非獨立結論）; it asks what to inspect and is not a standalone theorem.
The complete annotation and its linked argument form the acceptance unit.
Legacy Mode C skeletons remain supplemental and do not replace a source claim.

Mode C is a formatting/learning hypothesis, not proof of fewer regressions,
fixations or better reading speed. Tests must verify source HTML recoverability,
100% paragraph/annotation linking, heading hierarchy, anchor navigation,
highlight source linkage and safe unannotated fallback. Interactive scroll
observation is a view selection only, not a Four-Pass learner attempt.

## Admission to the 2000-word and 2000-sentence network

Target: **2,000 distinct English lexical items/phrases and at least 2,000 related complete engineering English sentences, accumulated across articles.** Source material determines the valid count per article, without invented filler. A candidate must be (a) tied to an engineering/concept decision, invariant, or runtime fact; (b) located in a specific source paragraph; (c) useful in spontaneous correct technical explanation; (d) paired with a grammatical source-faithful English sentence; (e) challengeable by a meaning-preserving prompt/oracle; and (f) deduplicated across articles by term + sense. Optional extra contexts do not create fake distinct entries.

Passive is broader exposure/recognition, not evidence of comprehension. Active is a *production target*, not a claim of performance. A short annotated article cannot be called a complete 2000-item corpus until 2000 independently admitted items and matching sentences actually exist.

## Four passes on one source

1. Recognize word form and short zh-TW contextual explanation.
2. Recognize decision, concept and runtime role in the **same original paragraph**.
3. Read/listen to the **same text**, keeping technical source/diagram available.
4. Generate a source-accurate English engineering sentence/explanation without copying; compare after attempted recall.

No `pass1/pass2/pass3` rewritten prose arrays, no second Medium article, no automatic practice events, no hidden application state in the article. The new static annotation overlay can use expandable optional oracles but cannot impersonate the frozen CEFR attempt-before-reveal native runtime. The four encounters are educational design rather than a neuroscience threshold.

Acceptance is source-byte preservation + 100% original paragraph annotation coverage + Source → Decision → Term → Sentence → Oracle linkage + PASSIVE/ACTIVE role integrity. Real learner mastery, measured latency and delayed recall remain NOT_OBSERVED without actual responses.

# LeetCode complete-article content profile — source of truth

## Selection and ownership

Use this profile only when a LeetCode/coding-interview task asks for a **complete, publishable Medium article** (including staged parts and final assembly). Ordinary `leetcode-mental` v4 exercises retain the 14-block / Five-Anchor / Four-Pass / Oracle contract in [v4-contract.md](v4-contract.md). Selecting the article profile changes the *presentation*, not algorithmic correctness or the user's opted-in learning mode.

For this profile, **leetcode-mental is the sole semantic Content Owner**: it produces and approves the entire source-grounded English technical narrative and the full Traditional Chinese final draft, including examples, reference code, decisions, invariants, proof, runtime internals, alternatives, complexity, limits, figures and interview content. It owns approval of any changes suggested by sloptrim, translation or semantic review.

**medium-writing is the Medium formatter and assembler** for an already approved article edition. It owns Medium-native headings, readable code and figure placement, captions/alt text placement, contiguous delivery parts, and the existing CLI's legal Stage 0–7 admission/assembly. It may not invent facts, delete qualifications, paraphrase protected code, shorten the article as a summary, or editorially rewrite accepted content. A content defect goes back to leetcode-mental for a new approved edition; do not use Stage 7 as a repair step. For non-LeetCode routes, medium-writing's existing writer ownership is unchanged.

The `alg-four` annotation owner is downstream only: it reads the accepted article bytes and adds Passive/Active notes without rewriting the base article. Neither this profile nor the formatting stage creates a Four-Pass learner session, runtime mastery evidence, new CLI stage, or publication authority.

## Construct the reasoning, then check coverage

Use [the article construction method](article-construction.md) to derive the
reader's questions, prerequisite relations, worked states, correctness argument
and cost explanation from the current problem. Its final-body reconstruction
checks each method and conditional adaptation actually introduced, before
English approval and again where editing changes its premises. Supporting
passages must allow the cost inference to be rebuilt from explained premises
or explicit elementary cost assumptions; quotation presence is not completion.
It applies without a polished example. The following coverage list checks the resulting
article; it does not replace construction with a topic checklist.

## Required complete content, not fixed headings

From the *actual* problem statement and assumptions derive a connected, zero-context explanation. Preserve, where applicable:

1. Contract: task, input/output, constraints, success condition, tricky inputs and mutation permission.
2. Reader decision chain: decision question, competing methods, governing constraint/invariant, why the choice follows, and a falsifier. Number of decisions is source-derived, not fixed by a past problem or a five-question writing lens.
3. Meaning of representation: canonical key, state, ownership and identity when relevant. Distinguish task-equivalence properties from the checkpointed loop invariant used in correctness proof.
4. One discriminating input-to-output **Program Movie**: exact state before/after material operations, branches, mutation, data-structure or API boundaries, return. Explain a key runtime fact where its behavior changes a decision; do not produce a glossary as a substitute for causal transitions.
5. Complete, readable Python 3 solution consistent with the trace; initial state, operation order, invariant/proof (initialization, maintenance, termination where applicable), minimal counterexample to a real incorrect approach, one changed-constraint pivot.
6. Independently derived time and space complexity with variables, loops, allocations and assumptions, including output versus auxiliary space when relevant; avoid treating a mental trace as execution evidence.
7. A relevant alternative and its trade-off. Clearly name the constraint under which it becomes preferable.
8. Concise English interview Q&A *grounded in the approved technical claims*, plus a closing zero-context Master Map that only connects facts already established.

This is a **content coverage contract**, not eight mandatory section names. The number of sections is determined by the actual reader decisions and distinct runtime boundaries, not a default quota. Build a single causal narrative in natural paragraphs. Merge passages only when they perform the same teaching work, **without dropping examples, intermediate states, derivations, limitations, proof obligations or decision outcomes**. For the Medium edition do not force the ordinary v4 fourteen pedagogical blocks into fourteen article headings; Four-Pass exercise material remains on the separate selected teaching route.

## Reader prerequisites and explanatory steps

Fix the actual audience before choosing detail. A reader who knows basic Python syntax
does not thereby know hashability, a library factory, a data-structure operation or a
logarithmic cost derivation. Naming a mechanism, stating its result or linking to a
source does not explain it. Supply the missing steps where that reader would otherwise
have to obtain the answer from prior knowledge.

Separate **algorithm decisions** from **teaching steps**. One design choice can require
several explanations: what information an object represents, why the next operation is
valid, its input state, the operation itself, its returned value or mutation, and the
effect on the next operation. A small decision count does not justify compressing those
steps into one paragraph. Use prose and worked states as needed; neither a sentence per
operation nor a fixed section count is required.

When a complete reference is supplied, read its body and account for its material
explanations, examples and derivations before drafting. Correct technical mistakes while
preserving their teaching purpose. A previously unreadable external link is not a reason
to ignore a later user-supplied full text. A requested API or runtime mechanism remains
in scope if the author chooses an equivalent implementation; changing code cannot silently
remove the teaching requirement. Explain that mechanism and show how it relates to the
chosen solution, or resolve a real scope conflict with the user.

Keep purposeful recurrence. Explaining a mechanism, following it with concrete values,
mapping it to complete code, and recalling it in concise interview English have different
reader purposes even when they mention the same fact. Preserve the necessary bridge in
each context; remove verbatim repetition that does no additional teaching work. This does
not require every concept to appear a fixed number of times. A Master Map may compress
previously explained relations, but cannot supply an explanation missing from the body.

Before accepting an editorial deletion, test the result against this reader and the
requested source coverage. Can the reader derive the next state and explain why it
follows, using the remaining article alone? If not, restore or rewrite the bridge.
Preserving the conclusion, technical terms and code is insufficient. Keep this semantic
review outside copyable prose; the detector, heading count, paragraph count and digest
cannot certify it.

## Language, editorial review and evidence

1. Produce the **entire English technical content** for the declared scope before formatting or translating. A source-bound incremental unit is allowed only if its place in the complete plan and pending coverage is recorded; a Boot Batch is not a completed article.
2. Apply the installed upstream `sloptrim` and its reader-article supplement to the English content **before translating**, when this execution host can actually run it. The Content Owner reviews every proposed change against technical claims, negation, conditions, versions, examples and code; `clean` is a style diagnostic, not semantic acceptance. If execution is unavailable, mark `NOT_RUN` and do not claim success.
3. Approve English content on semantic grounds. Translate that approved complete text to natural **Traditional Chinese with exact English technical terms** (and unchanged identifiers, source links, code, quantities and qualifications). Have the Content Owner check decision-bearing and exception-bearing English/zh-TW passages against the same pinned sources. Distinguish author's check from independent reader review.
4. Approve a **single complete Traditional Chinese content edition** before the formatter partitions or admits it. Do not let each delivery part become a different writer's or earlier draft's edition.
5. Preserve source locators, counterexamples, unknowns and evidence status. Source descriptions, algorithm traces, actually executed tests, learner achievement, CLI receipts and Medium publication are different kinds of evidence.

## Figure and article handoff

Figures are derived from material reader questions and runtime boundaries, not a universal count. For each necessary figure preserve: its unique conceptual purpose, supported nodes/edges and state values, exact article insertion anchor, caption and alt text in the approved language, and a self-contained rendering brief. Label illustrative complexity diagrams as conceptual rather than exact runtime traces. Explain every nontrivial diagram edge in the article or point to its explicit section. Avoid compressed vocabulary clouds or one poster containing all internals.

A cover is optional; figure image generation is **not** mandatory. Generate image assets only when the user requests them. When requested, produce individually usable figures in the requested count/order and review each for source-fidelity, legibility and correct terms; do not pretend a collage is multiple ready-to-insert files.

Handoff to medium-writing contains the approved full English and zh-TW narratives, source/claim coverage and unresolved limits, complete reference code, ordered section plan, figure positions/captions/alt text/briefs, and the actual editorial/execution evidence status. This is a semantic handoff description **using existing article/coverage/CLI inputs**, not a new persistent schema, state machine or invented hash/digest. Deterministic byte IDs come only from the original CLI/producer.

## Website-ready handoff when website delivery is selected

Supply both complete approved Markdown editions and the article-list data in
[the existing bilingual website contract](../../../../docs/bilingual-articles.md):
one stable slug, each language's title and short source-faithful description,
and the exact repository source paths. Titles must match their edition's H1;
do not put registry metadata, review notes or generated HTML into the prose.
The Content Owner approves both descriptions as well as the unchanged bodies.
An already approved edition can be handed off without reauthoring it; retain
its original draft, review and failure evidence separately.

Use the site's explicit article registry. Do not publish by scanning evaluation
directories or treating every generated draft as an accepted article.
The formatter/build owner preserves the supplied Markdown, renders separate
language routes and their own heading contents, and connects the article list,
language links and source downloads. Missing titles, descriptions or a complete
language edition return to the Content Owner; a build or navigation defect

## Part delivery and Stage boundary

The existing medium-compiler **Stage 0–7 remains unchanged**. Leetcode-mental supplies content needed for those stages; medium-writing sends it through the actual legal CLI steps and preserves source/code semantics. Stage 6 for this profile is a format-preserving pass over already approved wording (not a second editorial author); Stage 7 copies admitted bytes. Existing-article revisions follow the CLI's supported `init --draft` or authorized technical correction route; do not fabricate historical stages.

`Part 1..Part N` are **contiguous slices of one approved edition**, not new versions of authoring Stages 1..N. Use actual manifest/CLI output to pin order and exact bytes; place title only in Part 1, preserve complete code fences, number headings consistently, never duplicate sections or continuation narration within pasteable prose. If deduplication requires changing approved content, return to leetcode-mental and reapprove **before** Stage 7.

The assembled Medium result must contain the complete approved article once, with figure slots at the agreed positions, and no private sidecars, audit IDs, placeholders not intentionally marked as figure slots, or "continue?" chatter. Medium formatting does not prove semantic correctness, actual rendering, publication or learner comprehension.

## Minimal acceptance and stopping rule

Before handoff, check that an unfamiliar reader can reconstruct: goal and constraints; each material decision; why the representation works; an actual input-to-output trace; relevant language/runtime mechanism; alternative and failure case; cost derivation; full code/proof; what is a mental demonstration versus a test. Use another problem with different constraints in focused regression/evals to ensure no solution-specific fixed alphabet, key, Big O, section count or figure count leaks into the general profile.

Acceptance claims must separate `CONTENT_REVIEWED`, `SLOPTRIM_RUN/NOT_RUN`, `TRANSLATION_REVIEWED`, `CLI_VALIDATED`, `RUNTIME_TESTED/NOT_RUN`, `INDEPENDENT_READER/NOT_RUN`, `IMAGES_RENDERED/NOT_RUN` and `PUBLISHED/NOT_RUN`. These are reporting labels, **not** new CLI statuses.

Stop cognitive recursion once no new source-grounded, falsifiable issue could change scope, owner, behavior or verification. Do not re-run thinking methods as ceremony.

For speed-reading-authored notes, the complete annotation is the acceptance unit:
show source-bound premises and any state/order checkpoint before the short
reading cue (閱讀提示，非獨立結論). A source citation alone does not explain why
its premise matters. Follow the speed-reading Owner contract; the UI/validator
checks presence and exact bindings, while Owner/Reader review completeness.

## Reader-visible behavior

Traditional Chinese uses `/articles/<slug>/`; English uses
`/articles/<slug>/en/`. The home page and `/articles/` list the article with
both language links. Each page has its own title, description, document language,
a centered reading column, language switch and Markdown download. A collapsed
middle-right rail shows one bar per top-level chapter, including the introduction;
bar length encodes rendered text amount. Hover/click opens a scrollable dialog
with heading hierarchy, every paragraph, current location and its reviewed note.
The dialog shows chapter/paragraph counts. Touch/keyboard do not depend on hover;
Escape/close restores focus. Heading navigation selects the first following
paragraph. Contents and notes use the same source anchors. English reading annotations use
[the speed-reading method](../.agents/skills/speed-reading/SKILL.md); reviewed
formatting is stored on the existing paragraph sidecar and rendered locally.
No browser/CI model calls or dictionary requests are introduced. A plain-English
fallback is required when reviewed chunks or stress evidence are absent. Headings inside code fences do not enter the contents.
Contents links have unique targets even when headings repeat.

The global site's existing navigation and styling remain shared. This feature
does not translate the entire site. speed-reading owns the reviewed paragraph/Passive/Active annotation content;
ALG Four owns its source binding, admission validation and navigation;
the builder reuses its validator/projection for each explicitly registered article.
Language switching goes to the other complete edition; it does not invent a
paragraph alignment or claim a corresponding scroll position.
